items.briefing:
An Australian bank has taken steps to block staff from accidentally sharing confidential data with public AI tools — a timely reminder that using everyday AI chatbots for work tasks carries real privacy risks. Separately, a Spanish organisation was breached by an AI agent that modified personal data, showing that AI-powered attacks are becoming more sophisticated and can cause direct harm beyond simple data theft.

With digital money transfers growing unevenly across Asia Pacific, Australians sending money overseas should stay alert to scams targeting these platforms. **Practical tip:** Avoid pasting sensitive work information — client details, financial data, or internal documents — into public AI tools like ChatGPT. Use only approved, organisation-provided systems for work tasks.

featured.title: AI Agent Breaches Spanish Organization, Modifies Personal Data
featured.summary: AI-driven cyberattacks used to be exotic. Soon, it'll be odd if threat actors aren't using agents to do all of their bidding.
